claims.text: High-throughput computational screening can be used to discover new alloys.
High-throughput computational screening can identify alloys with optimized high-temperature oxidation resistance.
High-throughput computational screening can identify alloys with optimized phase stability.
The proposed method applies to metallic or ceramic materials.
Alloy microstructure and composition mediate the targeted oxidation resistance and phase stability.
Computational screening identifies new alloys with optimized properties.
The screened alloys are predicted to have improved high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The screened alloys are predicted to have improved phase stability.
Existing alloys have limited high-temperature oxidation resistance and phase stability.
The applicability of the method is bounded by high-temperature conditions, available computational resources, and alloy composition.
The accuracy of computational models and availability of computational resources create uncertainty in the prediction.
The computational predictions can be tested by comparison with experimental measurements of oxidation resistance, phase stability, microstructure, and composition.
